task: This is a synthetic newspaper-writing exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes. Write from the reporting snapshot as of August 3, 2026. Write a headline and a 450–650-word AP-style newspaper explainer using Fen Orchard Farm's carrot harvest to answer why a grower can lose sales without qualifying for a payment under a yield-based crop policy.

facts.text: Fen Orchard Farm harvested 36 tons of carrots in July 2026 but lost a planned buyer for ten tons shortly before collection.
The farm's supplied policy with Field Lantern Mutual covers specified weather-related yield losses, not every reduction in sales revenue.
The policy's insured reference yield is 40 tons, with a covered-yield threshold of 75%, or 30 tons, under the stated conditions.
The 36-ton harvest is above that threshold, and the insurer says the buyer's cancellation is not itself a covered yield event.
The policy is not described as revenue insurance or insurance against a customer's business failure.
The canceled buyer was a restaurant supplier that reduced its purchasing schedule; no insolvency finding is supplied.
Of the canceled ten tons, the farm resold three, donated four and composted three after it could not find another outlet.
The other 26 harvested tons went to the farm's remaining planned customers.
Unsold harvested carrots do not become unharvested crop merely because they generate no sale.
Grower Bela Orr said the harvest required the same planting, lifting and washing work even though part of its expected revenue disappeared.
Orr said, "We had the carrots. What vanished was the place they were supposed to go."
The farm has not disclosed a complete loss calculation covering resale prices, donations, disposal and saved delivery costs.
Mutual representative Neri Selt said, "A policy has to name the event it is covering, not just the fact that a season was expensive."
The mutual's explanation concerns this supplied policy and does not establish the terms of every agricultural insurance product.
A growers' association is collecting members' examples of canceled orders to discuss shared cold storage and alternative buyers.
No shared-storage project has been financed, and extra storage would not guarantee a later sale.
The donation recipient, Cedar Spoon Kitchen Network, accepted four tons for its scheduled meal operations rather than paying the farm's original contract price.
The record supplies no tax valuation or reimbursement for those donated carrots.
Fen Orchard grows vegetables despite its historical farm name, which dates to an earlier fruit operation.
There is no court or regulator ruling about the insurer's handling of this account in the reporting packet.

forbidden_additions: All unsold crop is a covered yield loss or every farm policy excludes revenue risks
A buyer insolvency, final financial loss, donation tax value or regulatory ruling not supplied

The 36-ton harvest exceeds the stated 30-ton threshold; sales and yield are separate measures.
